items.stem: What is the main purpose of a stage gate in product development?

options.text: A decision point to continue, pivot or stop based on evidence
options.rationale: Correct: gates force an evidence-based go/no-go before more is invested.

options.text: A place to finalise the marketing logo
options.rationale: Branding is one input, not the purpose of a gate.

options.text: A step where engineering is forbidden
options.rationale: Gates govern decisions; they do not ban work.

options.text: A legal requirement for all products
options.rationale: Stage gates are a management practice, not a legal mandate.

items.explanation: Correct: gates force an evidence-based go/no-go before more is invested.

items.stem: Which TWO are signs of a well-written product requirement? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: a good requirement can be verified objectively.

options.text: It states the need, not a specific solution
options.rationale: Correct: solution-free requirements leave room for better concepts.

options.text: It names the exact supplier part number
options.rationale: That over-specifies a solution too early.

options.text: It is intentionally vague to stay flexible
options.rationale: Vague requirements cannot be tested or agreed.

items.explanation: Correct: a good requirement can be verified objectively.

items.stem: You have limited time and one very uncertain assumption about user behaviour. What should your first prototype do?

options.text: Test the riskiest assumption as cheaply as possible
options.rationale: Correct: prototyping retires the biggest risk first with least cost.

options.text: Perfect the final finish and packaging
options.rationale: Finish work is wasted until the core risk is retired.

options.text: Build the full product to production quality
options.rationale: That is slow and expensive before the risk is understood.

options.text: Skip prototyping and go straight to launch
options.rationale: That leaves the biggest uncertainty untested.

items.explanation: Correct: prototyping retires the biggest risk first with least cost.
